subject: FY28 goal framing & budget storm — Ops/QBR prep
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: FinanceOps <financeops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FY28 goal framing & budget storm — Ops/QBR prep

Team —

We need to lock the frontal assumptions for FY28 so we can get a clean QBR narrative and the board-facing slides ready. Objectives for this thread:

- Surface three fiscal scenarios (growth / base / conservative) with top-line targets and the primary drivers for each.
- Capture headcount and COGS implications by org (Product, Infra, Go-to-Market).
- Identify up to three programmatic risks we should model and mitigations.
- Agree on schedule for a leadership workshop next week to finalise the slate.

I attached a simple workbook with tabs per org — FY27_vs_FY28_scenarios.xlsx — and a short QBR prep brief (QBR_prep_brief.pdf) that lays out the narrative framing we should aim for. Please:

1) Fill your org tab with baseline numbers + high/low levers by EOD Monday (2026-10-05) in the shared sheet. If you want, add a 1-line rationale for each delta.
2) Add your top-3 risks in the Risks tab.
3) Call out any continental/regional constraints (APAC capacity, EU data regs) that materially change the numbers.

I will consolidate inputs and run a 90-minute framing workshop with the leadership team on Wednesday 2026-10-07 10:00–11:30 PT (proposed) — will send a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Attachments: FY27_vs_FY28_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet), QBR_prep_brief.pdf (pdf)

Why this matters: we have an exec QBR two weeks after the workshop and the board pack needs a single scenario we recommend (with contingency lanes). The sooner we get good inputs the more time we have to stress-test assumptions.

Thanks — please be crisp.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
CEO, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FY28 goal framing & budget storm — Ops/QBR prep

Vivek — thanks for the clear ask. A few quick points / questions from Product: 

- I started a first-pass in the workbook (tab: ProductGrowth). High-level anchors: Growth = +68% ARR (aggressive GTM + expansion), Base = +40% ARR, Conservative = +18% ARR (slower enterprise ramp). Numbers assume current average deal size and a 20% improvement in self-serve conversion for the Growth lane.
- Headcount plan: Product is assuming +6 FTEs (3 PM, 2 Eng IC, 1 UX) in Growth; Base reduces hiring to +3; Conservative is hiring freeze. Please call out if Finance needs a different comp/overhead profile.
- Risk to model: 1) Delay in model onboarding for a large customer (timing risk), 2) GPU price volatility (cost risk), 3) Slow self-serve conversion (demand risk).

Question for FinanceOps (cc): what is the preferred cadence for headcount ramp phasing in the workbook — monthly or quarterly? For planning we usually model quarterly but fine with a monthly stub if the model needs it.

I’ll add short rationale bullets in the sheet by Monday.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product 
Redwood Inference

Great start, Marissa. A couple of operational callouts from the infra/capacity side: 

- Cost levers: GPU spot mix vs reserved; growth lane assumes 25% spot usage and aggressive autoscaling. If we change to 10% spot, unit COGS goes up ~12–15% — call that out as a sensitivity.
- Latency SLA tradeoffs: to hit the Growth revenue profile we need to accept 5–10% higher tail latency on low-tier routes unless we increase reserved capacity. That has product and CS implications.
- Headcount: infra is budgeting +4 SREs in Growth; Base keeps +2 and Conservative keeps headcount flat. We should show both hiring cash-flow and the steady-state run-rate.

Practical ask: can Product and GTM add a single-line note in your tabs on how latency / SLA changes materially impact conversion or churn? That will make the tradeoff visible for the exec narrative.

— Jonas
VP, Infrastructure Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the early inputs. Quick consolidation and next steps from Finance:

- Laura and I will standardize the headcount cost assumptions (comp, burden, ramp month) and populate the Finance tab by EOD Monday (2026-10-05).
- We’ll run two sensitivity views in the workbook: a unit-cost sensitivity (GPU pricing / cloud premium) and a conversion sensitivity (self-serve uplift +/- 10/20pp).
- Scheduling: Vivek, I’ll calendar a 90-minute leadership framing workshop on Wed 2026-10-07 10:00–11:30 PT. Agenda: 1) Confirm recommended scenario, 2) Decide 2 contingency lanes + triggers, 3) Assign owners for board pack slides. Please let me know if the time conflicts.

Deliverables I’ll own before the meeting: consolidated workbook (one tab per org + assumptions) and a 2-page exec memo summarising the recommended scenario and three primary risks. I’ll drop both into the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4FY28Planning

If ACME finance (cc’d) wants to see early numbers for contract planning we can share the Growth/Base rows as an interim.
